rules.title: Every Theme You Ship Must Work
Every Decision Must Have a Reason (Write It Down)

deliveryGate.title: Block 3: Liveliness (required to be alive, not just clean)

patterns.name: Generic Blue-Purple Gradient
patterns.tell: blue-to-purple, blue-to-cyan, or purple-to-pink gradients used as the primary color treatment, or a full-page colored glow.

patterns.name: Excessive Glassmorphism
patterns.tell: blur/backdrop-filter on the navbar, cards, modals, and sidebar at the same time.

patterns.name: Excessive Border Radius
patterns.tell: every element is pill-shaped: buttons, inputs, cards, badges, modals.

patterns.name: Overly Soft Shadows
patterns.tell: every component carries a large shadow, so the whole page feels like it is floating.

patterns.name: Glow Everywhere
patterns.tell: glow on cards, buttons, icons, badges, backgrounds, and borders simultaneously.

patterns.name: Background Grid
patterns.tell: grid squares, blueprint lines, graph paper, dot grids, or thin repeating lines behind content.

patterns.name: Dark Mode Default for No Reason
patterns.tell: the whole page is dark simply because it looks "tech", with no branding consideration.

patterns.name: Too Many Colors in the Palette
patterns.tell: 5-7 different colors on one page with no clear design system.

patterns.name: Excessive Accent Color
patterns.tell: one accent color on buttons, icons, badges, links, lines, backgrounds, and glows at once.

patterns.name: Sterile Default
patterns.tell: flat white or near-white, thin grey borders, small radius, no texture, generic font, no identity.

patterns.name: Monotonous Template Layout
patterns.tell: hero, subtitle, 2 CTAs, screenshot, feature grid, testimonials, FAQ, CTA, footer, in that order, every time.

patterns.name: Copy-Paste Feature Cards
patterns.tell: identical size, height, icon, layout, and padding across all feature cards.

patterns.name: Bento Grid
patterns.tell: a section made of a mosaic of differently-sized cards, some spanning two columns or two rows, filling the space like a tiled dashboard.

patterns.name: Uniform Spacing
patterns.tell: padding, margin, and gaps are identical across every section.

patterns.name: "How It Works" Always 3 Steps
patterns.tell: round icon + number 1, 2, 3 + short text, always three steps, always the same shape.

patterns.name: "Trusted By" Logo Bar
patterns.tell: a row of generic company logos directly below the hero.

patterns.name: "Most Popular" Pricing Card
patterns.tell: the middle pricing tier always highlighted with a capsule badge.

patterns.name: Demo Without a Product
patterns.tell: the page sells a product that is never shown working: no real demo, no Terms of Service, no Privacy Policy, just promises.

patterns.name: 4-Column Template Footer
patterns.tell: Product / Company / Resources / Legal columns with no variation.

patterns.name: Uniform Section Rhythm
patterns.tell: every section is centered title + subtitle + identical card grid, with no variation.

patterns.name: Generic AI Icons
patterns.tell: sparkle, star, magic, lightning, diamond, cube, robot, or AI orb as feature icons.

patterns.name: Lucide Icons
patterns.tell: every icon comes from the same thin-stroke, rounded-corner library (Lucide or a visual clone), so all icons share one recognizable look.

patterns.name: Emoji as Decoration
patterns.tell: literal emoji scattered through the copy, headings, badges, and buttons: 🚀 in a headline, ✅ beside every feature bullet, 🔥 on a CTA, 📈 above a chart title.

patterns.name: Small Arrows on Every Button
patterns.tell: `→` or `↗` placed on almost every button as pure decoration.

patterns.name: Colored Left Stripe
patterns.tell: a thin colored vertical bar on the left edge of cards, list rows, or section headers, used as decoration.

patterns.name: AI Capsule Badges
patterns.tell: pill shape, thin border, glow, small dot, uppercase, containing "AI Powered", "Beta", "New".

patterns.name: Eyebrow Badge Above the Headline
patterns.tell: a small pill sitting directly above the H1, often with a dot and a thin border, holding a category label ("Aplikasi Tagihan UKM", "The platform for teams") that the headline beneath it already says.

patterns.name: Decorative Status Dot
patterns.tell: a small colored dot beside a heading, eyebrow, nav item, or label, usually glowing and pulsing on a loop, that marks nothing. It borrows the visual language of a live or recording indicator for a page where nothing is live.

patterns.name: Generic AI Typography
patterns.tell: large monospace headings, or uppercase labels with extreme letter-spacing ("HOW IT WORKS", "FEATURES").

patterns.name: Fake Terminal Window
patterns.tell: a styled terminal window with traffic-light dots, a prompt line, and typed-out commands, used as the hero or feature visual.

patterns.name: Illustrations With No Connection
patterns.tell: Undraw, Storyset, or generic 3D blob characters with no real connection to the product.

patterns.name: Dead Navigation
patterns.tell: navbar links to pages or sections that do not exist.

patterns.name: Non-Functional Controls
patterns.tell: buttons do nothing, dropdowns won't open, forms cannot submit.

patterns.name: Sections That Fill a Template
patterns.tell: a section exists because "every AI landing page has one", not because the content needs it.

patterns.name: Default Dashboard Shell
patterns.tell: left sidebar, top bar, four stat cards, a chart, a table. Chosen before anyone asked what the screen is for, and identical whether it manages invoices, patients, or servers.

patterns.name: Stat Cards With Invented Numbers
patterns.tell: a row of four cards reading 12,483 / 94.2% / $48.2K / 1,204, each with a green "+12% this week" delta.

patterns.name: Filler Activity Feed
patterns.tell: "Sarah Chen updated a document, 2 hours ago", repeated with rotating names and avatars.

patterns.name: Charts Without a Question
patterns.tell: a line or donut chart placed because the space looked bare, with a generic title ("Overview", "Performance") and no axis the reader can act on.

patterns.name: Generic Table Columns
patterns.tell: Name, Status, Date, Actions, whatever the rows actually are, with a three-dot menu on every row.

patterns.name: Filler Data in Fields and Columns
patterns.tell: empty form fields and table columns filled with fake but plausible data: `John Doe`, `johndoe@example.com`, `"Let's build something"`, phone numbers and dates that belong to nobody.

patterns.name: Placeholder Empty and Loading States
patterns.tell: "No data available" with an illustration, a bare spinner, or a full-page skeleton that mimics a layout the real data never fills.

patterns.name: Endless Pulses and Loops
patterns.tell: elements that pulse, bounce, or float forever with no user trigger.

patterns.name: Template Animations Stacked
patterns.tell: every element uses Fade Up + Fade In + Floating + Scale + Bounce simultaneously.

patterns.name: Empty AI Vocabulary
patterns.tell: verbs and abstract nouns stacked to sound impressive without saying anything: *unlock, elevate, empower, delve, showcase, testament, landscape (abstract), journey, robust, game-changer, next-level, seamless, cutting-edge, revolutionary*.

patterns.name: Significance Inflation
patterns.tell: "the future of X", "marking a pivotal moment", "a testament to", "revolutionizing", "a new era of".

patterns.name: Empty Claims and Social Proof with No Evidence
patterns.tell: "Trusted by thousands of teams", "industry-leading", "world-class", "loved by customers everywhere", with nothing named or verifiable.

patterns.name: Weasel Attributions
patterns.tell: "Experts say", "industry observers", "people report", "leading analysts believe", with no one named.

patterns.name: Persuasive Authority Tropes
patterns.tell: "at its core", "the real question is", "what really matters", "fundamentally", "the deeper issue", "the heart of the matter".

patterns.name: Chatbot Closers
patterns.tell: "I hope this helps!", "Let me know if you have any questions", "Would you like me to expand on this?", "You're welcome!".

patterns.name: Fake-Candid Openers
patterns.tell: "Honestly?", "Let's be honest", "Here's the thing", "Real talk", as a theatrical pause before an ordinary point.

patterns.name: Signposting Announcements
patterns.tell: "Let's dive in", "Here's what you need to know", "In this article we'll explore", "Without further ado".

patterns.name: All-Caps Emphasis
patterns.tell: a whole sentence, clause, or phrase in ALL CAPS inside a paragraph to shout emphasis: "The launch is ready and WE NEED TO MOVE NOW before the window closes."

patterns.name: Actorless Passive
patterns.tell: the passive voice with the actor deleted: "the decision was made to sunset the free tier", "the pricing page has been updated", "mistakes were made".

patterns.name: Inanimate Subject, Human Verb
patterns.tell: an abstraction given agency: "the data tells us", "the design decides", "the complaint becomes a fix", "the roadmap wants to focus on retention".

patterns.name: Rule of Three Overuse
patterns.tell: every idea forced into a group of three to sound complete: "innovation, inspiration, and insights".

patterns.name: Negative Parallelism and Tailing Negations
patterns.tell: "It's not just X, it's Y", "Not only X, but also Y", and clipped fragments tacked on as emphasis: "no guessing", "no wasted motion".

patterns.name: Aphorism Formulas
patterns.tell: "X is the language of Y", "X is the currency of Z", "X is not a tool but a mirror", "Efficiency becomes a trap when".

patterns.name: Staccato Drama
patterns.tell: a run of short declarative fragments to manufacture a punchline: "It had no preference. No prior. No nostalgia."

patterns.name: Synonym Cycling
patterns.tell: swapping synonyms to avoid repeating a word: "the protagonist faces a challenge, the main character must adapt, the central figure persists".

patterns.name: False Ranges
patterns.tell: "from X to Y" where X and Y are not on a meaningful scale: "from onboarding to scale", "from first click to final invoice, and everything in between".

patterns.name: Fabricated Specifics
patterns.tell: invented numbers, testimonials, names, dates, or features that look realistic but are not real.

patterns.name: Speculative Gap-Filling
patterns.tell: when the writer does not know a fact, they write a sentence about not knowing it, then invent plausible filler: "the company was likely founded in the 1990s", "she maintains a low profile".

patterns.name: Generic Positive Conclusion
patterns.tell: "The future looks bright", "Exciting times lie ahead", "This is a major step in the right direction".

patterns.name: Em Dashes
patterns.tell: the em dash character (`—`) used as an aside or connector: *"institutions — not the people — continue"*.

patterns.name: Boldface Overuse
patterns.tell: every key term bolded mechanically: "OKRs, KPIs, BMC".

patterns.name: Excessive Quotation Marks
patterns.tell: long text studded with quotation marks: quoting words that do not need quoting, scare quotes around ordinary terms, and quotes used as a default for emphasis or hedging. The page reads quoted rather than written.

patterns.name: Inline-Header Lists
patterns.tell: list items that start with a bolded header followed by a colon: "- User Experience: The UX has been improved".

patterns.name: Emojis in Headings
patterns.tell: decoration emojis leading headings or bullets: 🚀 Launch, 💡 Key insight, ✅ Next steps.

patterns.name: Filler Phrases
patterns.tell: "In order to" for "to", "Due to the fact that" for "because", "At this point in time" for "now", "It is important to note that" for nothing.

patterns.name: Excessive Hedging
patterns.tell: multiple qualifiers stacked on one claim: "could potentially possibly", "may perhaps".

patterns.name: Low-Contrast Text
patterns.tell: light grey text on a white or near-white background, thin body text, muted labels chosen because they look "elegant" but are hard to read.

patterns.name: Text Over a Photo or Gradient
patterns.tell: white text placed directly over an image or gradient that is light in some areas, checked at one bright spot only.

patterns.name: The Grey-on-Grey Hallucination
patterns.tell: "dark grey on black" or "light grey on white" claimed to pass AA without a computation.

patterns.name: Non-Text Contrast
patterns.tell: interactive components (buttons, icons, input borders, focus indicators, chart segments) distinguished from their background by less than 3:1.

patterns.name: Removed Focus Outline
patterns.tell: `outline: none` or `outline: 0` with no replacement focus style.

patterns.name: Mouse-Only Patterns
patterns.tell: menus that open on hover only, dropdowns that click-open but do not keyboard-open, drag-and-drop with no keyboard fallback.

patterns.name: Broken Tab Order
patterns.tell: focus jumps around the page, skips content, or lands on hidden elements because the DOM order does not match the visual order.

patterns.name: Weak or Invisible Focus Indicator
patterns.tell: a focus ring the same color as the background, a ring that only appears on hover, or an indicator thinner than a 1px border.

patterns.name: Color-Only Feedback
patterns.tell: success, error, and status communicated only by color: red error text, green success border, a tinted chip, with no icon, label, or text.

patterns.name: Missing UI States
patterns.tell: a data view with no empty, loading, or error state, or states that exist but are invisible: a spinner with no text, an empty screen with no explanation.

patterns.name: Text That Cannot Zoom
patterns.tell: fixed pixel font sizes, or containers with `overflow: hidden` that clip text at 200% zoom.

patterns.name: Mobile Keyboard Covers the Form
patterns.tell: inputs at the bottom of the viewport hidden behind the on-screen keyboard, with no scroll-into-view and no room for the input.

patterns.name: Desktop-Only Layout
patterns.tell: one layout state for every screen; the mobile view is the desktop layout squeezed into a phone.

patterns.name: Breakpoint Driven by Device List
patterns.tell: breakpoints named after phone widths (375px, 414px, 768px) chosen because "that is the iPhone size", not because the content breaks there.

patterns.name: Mobile Styled Last
patterns.tell: mobile rules bolted on as a trailing override: a long desktop stylesheet with a small media query at the end fixing one or two things.

patterns.name: Two-State Layout
patterns.tell: a layout with exactly two states: a single stacked column below one breakpoint, and a wide multi-column grid above it, with nothing defined in between. A tablet or small laptop width then inherits whichever state is closest: the phone stack stretched absurdly wide, or the desktop grid crammed into a fraction of its intended canvas.

patterns.name: Desktop-Sized Everything
patterns.tell: padding, gaps, hero heights, and card sizes carried unchanged from desktop to mobile, so every section looks blown up on a phone.

patterns.name: Fixed Pixel Type
patterns.tell: font sizes in fixed px that never change between desktop and mobile, so headings and body text stay oversized on a phone.

patterns.name: 100vh Sections
patterns.tell: hero and section heights set to `100vh`, so a section fills the whole phone screen and pushes everything else below the fold.

patterns.name: Huge Empty Padding
patterns.tell: desktop-scale section padding (96px, 128px) kept on mobile, creating tall empty gaps between sections on a phone.

patterns.name: Columns That Don't Collapse
patterns.tell: a multi-column grid keeps its side-by-side columns on mobile, so the columns shrink, the text wraps awkwardly, and elements collide.

patterns.name: Fixed-Width Grid
patterns.tell: `grid-template-columns` set in fixed px, or grid areas that cannot reflow, so the grid stays rigid when the viewport shrinks.

patterns.name: Forced 12-Column
patterns.tell: a 12-column grid forced onto mobile content that needs one or two columns, so spans look arbitrary and the math fights the layout.

patterns.name: Horizontal Scroll Leak
patterns.tell: the page scrolls sideways because some element is wider than the viewport: a table, a code block, an image, a long unbroken string.

patterns.name: Overflow Hidden Clipping
patterns.tell: `overflow: hidden` on a container that clips content at narrow widths, hiding text or controls instead of letting them fit.

patterns.name: Fixed-Width Children
patterns.tell: flex or grid children with a fixed px width or `min-width` that burst out of their parent on a narrow screen.

patterns.name: Under-Sized Targets
patterns.tell: buttons, links, and controls smaller than about 44 x 44 px, easy to hit on desktop with a cursor but hard to hit with a thumb.

patterns.name: Targets Too Close
patterns.tell: 44px targets packed together with no gap, so a thumb tap hits the wrong one.

patterns.name: Hover-Only Interactions
patterns.tell: menus, reveals, and tooltips that exist only on hover, so a touch user can never open them.

patterns.name: Nav That Stays Desktop
patterns.tell: the desktop top bar with its row of links kept side by side on mobile, so the links crowd, wrap into two rows, or spill past the viewport.

patterns.name: The Bare Hamburger
patterns.tell: everything hidden behind a hamburger icon with no label and no hint, so a user never realizes the menu exists or cannot tell what it opens.

patterns.name: Bottom Nav That Eats Content
patterns.tell: a fixed bottom nav bar that sits over the content, covering the last list items, the final button, or the form the user was trying to finish.

patterns.name: Sticky Nav Steals the Screen
patterns.tell: a sticky header or tall bottom bar that holds a large fixed height, so a big slice of the phone screen is always taken by navigation.

patterns.name: Decorative Separators
patterns.tell: banner comments built from repeated characters, ALL CAPS labels, or box drawing around a section name: `// =======================` around `Authentication`, `// -------- WORKFLOW --------`, or a `/* ---- ROUTES ---- */` header.

patterns.name: Restating the Obvious
patterns.tell: a comment that repeats what the next line or declaration already shows, like `// Initialize the variable` above `let count = 0`, `// User class` above `class User {}`, `// Validate user` above `function validateUser()`, or `const userAge = 25; // User age is 25`.

patterns.name: Workflow Narration
patterns.tell: comments that narrate the flow step by step, like `// Step 1: Validate input`, `// Step 2: Process request`, `// Step 3: Return response`, or `// First...`, `// Next...`, `// Finally...`.

patterns.name: Empty Labels
patterns.tell: generic labels with no information behind them: `// Main logic`, `// Core logic`, `// Business logic`, `// Helper function`, `// Entry point`, `// Error handling`, or `// Note: This is important.` / `// Important: Please read.`

patterns.name: Vague Placeholders
patterns.tell: comments that promise future work without saying what: `// TODO: Improve this`, `// Future improvements`, `// Additional optimization can be added here`, `// Add more validation`.

patterns.name: Signature Echo
patterns.tell: documentation that only restates the signature, like a JSDoc block that repeats `@param price The price.` and `@returns Total price.` for a function whose name and parameters already say all of it.

patterns.name: Decorative Emoji
patterns.tell: emoji used as decoration in comments, like `// ✅ Validation` or `// 🚀 Performance`.

patterns.name: End Markers
patterns.tell: comments that only mark the end of a block, like `} // end if`, `# End of function`, or `// End processOrder`.

patterns.name: The Over-Explained Comment
patterns.tell: one comment that runs on for several lines, stacking reasons, context, and history around a fact that fits in one line: a four-line block explaining that a stub sits on PATH, which release introduced the workaround, and what broke before it. Every sentence is true. The length is the tell.

patterns.name: Line-by-Line Narration
patterns.tell: a comment on every trivial statement, narrating each line as it is written: `// Initialize count`, then `// Loop items`, then `// Get item`, then `// Increment`, then `// Return result`.

patterns.name: Stiff or Loud Wording
patterns.tell: comments that sound formal, long, or shout: "This function is responsible for validating whether the supplied credentials are valid before continuing with the authentication process", or `// MAIN LOGIC` in caps.
